exposure: gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) status of the mother
neonatal birth weight category (fetal growth restriction, normal birth weight, macrosomia)
outcome: neonatal genetic metabolism (amino acids, free carnitine, acylcarnitine levels)
cohort: The study included 1252 GDM patients and their newborns diagnosed at Changzhou Maternal and Child Health Care Hospital from 2017 to 2021, categorized into three groups based on neonatal birth weight: fetal growth restriction, normal birth weight, and macrosomia.
finding: Gestational diabetes mellitus with different birth weights influences neonatal genetic metabolism in distinct ways, with specific amino acid and carnitine profiles differing across fetal growth restriction, normal birth weight, and macrosomia groups.
mod_finding: The fetal growth restriction group (G1) exhibited the highest rates of cesarean section compared to the normal birth weight (G2) and macrosomia (G3) groups.
birth_weight: Categorized as fetal growth restriction (G1), normal birth weight (G2), and macrosomia (G3), without specific weight ranges provided.
